arp._note: Populated by scripts/deploy/deploy.sh. Addresses are EOA-nonce-derived (CREATE), so re-running with a new nonce will produce different addresses. To redeploy, increment the nonce assumption — there is no on-chain idempotency guard.
arp._moduleRegistryNote: Redeployed 2026-06-03 with schemaURI uniqueness (ADR 0013). V1 address kept for historical reference; orphan (UI reads V2).

rigAgents._note: Task 24. ERC-8004 agents on ARP's own testnet registry, minted 2026-10-19 on chain 13579. SIGNED BY THE AGENT SESSION using the operator's PRIVATE_KEY from .env, on the user's explicit authorisation — not by a human at a keyboard. See ADR 0037. security.md scopes its automation prohibition to mainnet, so this is permitted and was previously unwritten. Agents 1 and 2 were left with an EMPTY tokenURI deliberately: no-token-uri is 23% of the real cohort (32/140, scripts/measure/cohort-endpoints.ts), so they exercise a branch the three new agents cannot. Permanent: the ids are taken and setAgentURI leaves the superseded URI in the mint transaction's calldata.

3._endpointNote: ARP's own MCP server, local by default. ARP_MCP_ENDPOINT regenerates the file and setAgentURI can update the agent — but that escape hatch is a rehearsal prop: portability.md rule 4 says any step that works because ARP can write to the registry is not a step, and on mainnet ARP owns no registry. The real fix is a public endpoint.
3._documentShaNote: sha256 of the data: URI, first 16 hex. Lets repo-vs-chain drift be detected: the fixtures in scripts/seed/rig-registration-files.ts are the source of truth for three permanent mints, and an edit to FILES would otherwise diverge silently. Checked by scripts/verify/verify-rig-claims.ts against a gate report. ONLY REPRODUCIBLE WITH ARP_MCP_ENDPOINT UNSET: OWN_ENDPOINT reads the environment and the document is hashed after substitution, so anyone with it exported sees a false DRIFT.

4._endpointNote: TEST-NET-1, RFC 5737 — reserved and never routable, so it always times out. A .invalid hostname was tried first and gave inconclusive/transport-error, because a DNS failure is indistinguishable from our own network being down.

5.exercises: not-checkable ×2 — templated and non-http-identifier. Never a defect.

gate.command: bun run scripts/verify/verify-cohort.ts --target intuition-testnet --ids 1,2,3,4,5 --tools --out /tmp/gate.json && bun run scripts/verify/verify-rig-claims.ts /tmp/gate.json
gate.result: 5 agents: 2 with no tokenURI (40%), 3 read. 4 endpoints: 2 confirmed (serves-declared-protocol, dead), 2 not-checkable (templated, non-http-identifier), 0 inconclusive, 1 capability list recovered (arp_tool_reputation).
gate._requires: apps/mcp/src/server.ts listening on :3002, or agent 3 reports inconclusive. The confirmed branch is therefore reproducible only on a host running that server — a known limit of this gate until ARP has a public endpoint.
gate._widerThanSpecced: --ids 1,2,3,4,5 rather than 3,4,5. Including the two empty-tokenURI agents exercises a fifth branch for two extra requests.
gate._claimsCheck: verify-rig-claims.ts asserts each fixture's `exercises` prose against the outcome the probe observed, and the document hashes against this file. The unit suite CANNOT close that class: confirmed and inconclusive are both probeable before a request is sent, and the mutation that actually shipped lived exactly there.
